name: Snell's Window
desc: The scene drops under the water and you look back up at the surface — the whole 180-degree sky refracts into one bright disc at the 48.6-degree critical angle, its horizon compressed into a burning gold rim, while everything outside the disc goes to total internal reflection and becomes a swimming silver-teal mirror; the chop tilts the surface so the window breathes, shreds and reassembles, and the sun wanders inside it throwing glitter along the rim.

energy.doc: sea state — chop amplitude, how hard the surface lenses and shreds the window rim, rim + sun brightness

scale.doc: window radius vs design size — 0.35 is a distant porthole, 2.2 floods the frame with sky

murk.doc: water turbidity — how opaque the total-internal-reflection mirror sits over the scene

alpha.doc: overall overlay opacity — drop toward 0.3 to leave the scene reading clearly

hue.doc: water hue — zenith and mirror; the compressed horizon rim swings warm off it

x.doc: window centre x (where you are looking straight up)

style.doc: aesthetic — daylight: warm sky disc over a silver-teal mirror · nocturne: night dive, cold silver window on near-black water · thermal: false-colour radiance map · schematic: optics-diagram contours, dashed critical circle and ray construction, no picture at all · ink: quantised sumi tones with a dry-brush surface

act.doc: multi-minute sea-state programme — calm: glassy, wide sharp window · chop: working surface, boundary breaking up · swell: long-period heave that opens and closes the window
